title: KPI Retrospective Journal — Priya
content:
Context: personal working doc for tracking KPIs and weekly check-ins. Mostly notes-to-self, rough numbers, and experiment ideas. Not polished — keep it lightweight and actionable.

High-level OKR drafts (working):
- Objective O1: Make hosted text-generation predictably fast and 3x cheaper at scale
  - KR1: Reduce 99th percentile tail latency (text-gen, 2k tokens) from ~950ms to <=800ms on p-prod hosted pool
  - KR2: Cut per-token serving cost for common web workloads by 10% via batching + cache improvements
  - KR3: Automate 2 rollout safety checks (latency and quality) in Redwood Console to reduce manual rollbacks by 30%

- Objective O2: Improve developer experience for private deployments
  - KR1: Ship v1 of simplified private deploy onboarding flow (docs + CLI) with <5 manual support touches on pilot
  - KR2: Add basic KMS integration doc + 1 end-to-end test with partner

Notes / Rationale:
- O1 is priority for hosted-api footprint where most variable costs live. Focus on 99p latency because it drives error budget and escalations.
- O2 is runway for Private product; lower priority but time-box a few items this quarter.

Current metrics snapshot (raw, approximate):
- Hosted p-prod (text-gen, baseline model): 50k qps aggregate across pools, median latency 120ms, p95 ~340ms, p99 ~950ms (peak observed during Apr bench).
- Per-token cost (observed avg for web routing): $0.0009/token — target $0.00081/token (-10%).
- Rollouts: ~6 manual rollbacks last quarter; 2 were infra flakiness, 4 were model quality regressions.

Week-by-week check-ins (selected excerpts):
- 2026-01-05: Quick sync after holiday. Sketch: KV prefix cache prototype looks promising on dev rigs. Bench shows 12% token cost reduction for short prompt traces. TODO: run on dedicated staging pool.
- 2026-01-19: Observed tail latency spike during Canary A on eu-west region. Suspect autoscaler cooldown + long-running batch. Action: add jitter to batch window and test.
- 2026-02-02: Paused rollout after quality regression on model-quantized v2. Need to add per-prompt eval set; reach out to Eval infra (Rae).
- 2026-02-24: Canary pass for batching tweak. p99 went from 880ms -> 760ms in controlled test for 2k sequence. Small regression in p50 due to extra serialization overhead for some paths.

Retrospective notes (mid-sprint):
- What worked:
  - Short experiments yielded measurable cost wins (KV cache + small batching changes).
  - Canary + immediate rollback prevented wider impact for model-quantized v2.
- What didn't:
  - Lack of automated per-prompt quality gating — we still rely on manual sampling.
  - Runbook gaps for region-specific autoscaling (eu-west incident).
- Improvements to try:
  - Add lightweight per-prompt automated eval that runs on canary samples (quick heuristics: perplexity delta + spot-check embeddings similarity)
  - Create a tiny chaos test for autoscaler: simulate 30% sudden load + short-lived worker drop to catch cooldown misconfigurations

Experiment backlog (prioritized):
1) KV prefix cache: stage -> dedicated staging -> measure 7-day cost delta (owner: Priya)
2) Batch window jittering + dynamic TTL: test on eu-west small pool (owner: Alex)
3) Quick per-prompt eval harness: basic impl in serving-runtime tests (owner: Rae)
4) Rollout automation: add automatic fallback to last-known-good model if p99 > threshold during canary (owner: Priya/Rae)

Open questions / blockers:
- Can we run the KV cache on the same worker CPU budget without affecting latency for long sequences? (need A/B)
- Who will maintain the per-prompt quick-eval after prototype? (Ops vs. Infra?)
- Legal asked about KMS design for private pilot — need a short writeup for security review (ticket: PLAT-5588).

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Run KV cache on dedicated staging pool and collect 7-day stats (Priya)
- Implement jitter + run chaos autoscaler test on eu-west (Alex)
- Wire a minimal eval hook into Canary pipeline (Rae + Priya)
- Draft KMS design note for security (1 pager, link to PLAT-5588)

Quick notes-to-self:
- Don’t over-optimize batching for datasets with extremely long sequences — prioritize short seq wins first.
- Keep instrumentation lightweight; cost to collect metrics can neutralize gains.
- Save a snapshot of the Canary logs for the eu-west incident (JIRA:PLAT-3421).

Meeting snippets / snippets to paste to manager before 1:1:
- Wins: KV cache prototype shows ~12% token cost reduction in dev benches; canary latency improved after batching tweak (p99 760ms test).
- Risks: No automated per-prompt quality gating; model quantized v2 rollback shows risk to user experience.
- Ask: 1) OK to carve out 30% sprint capacity for rollout automation? 2) Support from Eval infra to productionize quick-eval?

Random brainstorm (raw):
- Could we expose a "gravity score" for prompts that tells routing layer whether to prefer cached KV vs fresh? Might help route low-variance prompts to cheaper pools.
- Lightweight user-sampled quality app: ask 0.1% of requests for quick thumbs up/down for a week during canary to attach human signal to metrics. Privacy implications — ping Legal.

Changelog (doc):
- 2025-11-04: initial sketch of OKRs and metrics
- 2026-01-05: added KV cache bench notes + action items
- 2026-02-24: updated after successful batching canary; added next actions and blockers

End.
